column8: Mon 16 Nov: store, and a possible 2.0 detail: her five T-bonds (issued 2007-2011) were only ever entries on the Fed's books; the ledger sense of in ink is unverified, so no conceit turn rests on it.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; TRADES (effective 1 Jan 1997) is the one federal rule under every Treasury she holds, directly or through a fund; background for row 4.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q58-035, which already carries 31 U.S.C. 3123(a) read at source; re-read today, and the full sentence ends issued under this chapter; the only-promise framing lives in rows 35-36.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and 2.0; Treasury pays the clearing bank at the top with no action by anyone (31 CFR 357.13), which makes IPS l.13's Held to the end, these pay what they say literal; any later delay is an intermediary's.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 definition and 3e; the exact answer to whose promise the ink is: the Treasury's, held for her through a chain, never a promise made to her by name.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the chain's top tier; the 2,300 participants figure is from 2008, never printed as current.
Mon 16 Nov: the legal name (security entitlement) behind row 8; one clause carries both, so merged into the stronger row 8.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 definition and 3d; UCC 8-503 re-read at source today, quotes exact: owned is the law's own word; quote with its opening To the extent necessary and the 8-511 exception, or paraphrase.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the broker's three duties (obtain and keep, no liens without consent, collect from the issuer) carry each maturity to her account; a duty, not a guarantee.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; the use line overstates: under 8-511(b) a lender with control wins if the broker breaks its duty, so the protection is the duty plus Rule 15c3-3 and SIPA (rows 11-13), not 8-511.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e; closes the SEC-rules-not-read gap in Q26-022 and Q8a-025; but the IPS never says it borrows nothing (l.11 says anybody else's money): say the plan buys only with her deposits, so every holding is fully paid.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e; in a broker failure customers first share the segregated pool and the trustee can move accounts without asking; pairs with row 13.

Mon 16 Nov: corrects store Q30-034 (custody is the weakest row; also Q3b-031, Q8a-025, SKELETON item 4(c)): SIPC's cap limits only its advance above her ratable share, so on a $589,655 claim she loses only if the pool returns under about 15% (Keel arithmetic); drop $89,655 at risk ($589,655 is 8k's all money at the end, about $474,000 after the contribution); custody is a 3e line, not a Table 3 row.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e base rate; SIPC's own undated record says broker failures are delays, almost never losses; MJK's accounts moved in about a week.

Mon 16 Nov: re-read at source today (LBI from Fri 19 Sep 2008, closed 28 Sep 2022, $106bn, 111,000 claims, most within weeks); same release as row 16, which carries the stronger contrast; adds final figures to store Q2a-022.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and 3d's owned, not owed; re-read today: both figures are Lehman Brothers Inc., the broker (customers 100% with no Government or SIPC money; unsecured general creditors 41.2841%, $9.372bn, at the close); say general creditors, never lenders, never beside the ETN's 44.5% (the parent LBHI).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e's honest residual is time: MF Global's 330 retail securities accounts moved 39 days after the trustee (Keel arithmetic checks), so only a late-year failure could hold a 1 January payment.

Mon 16 Nov: store; 886 days (checks) was the last distribution, futures customers included; securities customers were satisfied early (Q2a-022), so never say a securities customer waited two and a half years, as claim 2's verdict implies.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and SKELETON 4(c)'s December 2032 cash; money waiting in the short-term Treasury ETF (TNA l.5) is held for her, broker cash is owed to her under SIPC's $250,000 cash limit; claim, not property overstates (cash shares in the 15c3-3 reserve and the pool, rows 11-12).
Mon 16 Nov: wording rule for 2.0 and 3e: held for her, never in her name; Cede & Co. is record owner of the fund shares and VT, while the T-bonds sit on the Fed's books in a clearing bank's account.
Mon 16 Nov: store; fund shares settle through DTC, a link the T-bonds lack; 2016 iShares text, the 2026 Treasury iBonds passage unread.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 definition and Table 1; Declaration s.3.08 re-read today, quotes exact; the trustees hold the Treasuries for the trust and she owns a share of that pool, so owned in Treasuries holds for the fund rows; 2009 text, check for a later restatement.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e; s.2.07 re-read today: IBTM's Treasuries cannot pay another iShares fund's debts; s.3804's conditions (separate records, notice in the certificate) unread, so S 4.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e; the 1940 Act puts the fund's Treasuries with a custodian bank, never on BlackRock's books; one clause with rows 22-23.
Mon 16 Nov: store; say a custodian bank, never a named bank: the Treasury iBonds' 2026 custodian is unverified.
Mon 16 Nov: store or one 3e clause; the only bank credit inside a fund is brief cash at its custodian; size unread, so no Table 3 row.
Mon 16 Nov: store; an absence in statements read in part, as of 31 Oct 2025; never say IBTM does not lend (Q26-014 keeps lending losses inside the 0.5% cut).
Mon 16 Nov: the same prospectus quotes as Q16-001 (and H3-007); the nobody-promises framing is row 37's.
Mon 16 Nov: store; a sponsor change ends the advisory contract and needs a holders' vote while the fund's assets stay put; not one of the IPS's two reasons.
Mon 16 Nov: store; her funds' sponsor changed hands once (Barclays to BlackRock, 2009) and the funds ran on; proxy filed by iShares, Inc., date inferred.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e clause; a fund sponsor's parent went bankrupt (Lehman, 2008) and its funds' adviser carried on; that the assets were safe is inference, the supplement is silent on them.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e or 2.2 aha (an ETN owes, an ETF owns); FWP wording verified; 44.5% is etf.com's secondary figure for the parent LBHI's senior creditors by 2018, payments continuing, on $13.5m mostly seed money: say by 2018, never in 2008, never beside LBI's 41.28%.
Mon 16 Nov: store; VT has no promise at the top, pencil by design until half moves (IPS l.15); check whether $90,207m is the whole fund or VT's share class.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; implementation, never a change to the frozen plan; transfer-in rules unverified.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e and IPS l.11; no holder in the chain puts its own money behind a payment; the LBI release adds that its customers were paid without Government or SIPC money.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e footnote; names the plan's real exposures as AHA_REGISTER reserve 5b asks (one promise, the rest holders); counts are simplified, so say holders, not a number.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 and 3e; Caplet's definition holds in law for every Treasury row: keep CONCEIT V2.1's words, add the chain once in 3e; a fund's payout never fixed (TNA l.15).
